method: Sources were opened and read at a stated locator. Metadata, abstracts, search snippets, dictionary entries and landing pages are not inspection. No access control was bypassed.

inspections.sourceIdentity: JCGM 200:2012, International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM), 3rd edition
inspections.locator: §2.41 (6.10), definition of metrological traceability, with Note 1.
inspections.accessBasis: Published by the BIPM Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology, freely available.
inspections.reuseBasis: Reference-only. Bounded original summary; the definition is not reproduced verbatim.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That metrological traceability is a property of a measurement result: the result can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to the measurement uncertainty.
inspections.boundary: This is traceability of a measurement to a reference standard. It is not provenance of a document, lineage of a citation, or an audit trail of a system, all of which share the word. A page about record traceability must not cite this definition.
inspections.relationshipToEarlier: Carried forward into Tranche 17 via Tranche 16: same source, same locator, same claim scope. Originally inspected as tr16-src-101.

inspections.sourceIdentity: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management
inspections.locator: Executive Summary, paragraph placing incident response across the six CSF 2.0 Functions.
inspections.accessBasis: United States government publication, freely available.
inspections.reuseBasis: US government work; bounded original summary with attribution.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That incident response is treated as part of cybersecurity risk management rather than a standalone activity, and is distributed across the Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover functions.
inspections.boundary: Recommendations and considerations, not a reporting obligation. It sets no disclosure deadline, names no regulator, and does not establish when an incident must be reported to anyone.
inspections.relationshipToEarlier: Carried forward into Tranche 17 via Tranche 16: same source, same locator, same claim scope. Originally inspected as tr16-src-102.

inspections.sourceIdentity: JCGM 200:2012, International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM), 3rd edition
inspections.accessBasis: Published by the BIPM Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology, freely available.
inspections.reuseBasis: Reference-only. Bounded original summary; the definition is not reproduced verbatim.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That measurement error is the measured quantity value minus a reference quantity value, and therefore presupposes a reference against which the measurement is compared.
inspections.boundary: Error in the metrological sense, requiring a reference value. It is not model error, prediction error, or a mistake in a procedure, and it does not define uncertainty, which the same vocabulary treats as a separate concept.
inspections.relationshipToEarlier: Third definition read from the document already inspected for calibration in Tranche 15 and traceability in Tranche 16.

inspections.sourceIdentity: W3C PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
inspections.locator: Bundle definition — a named set of provenance descriptions that is itself an entity.
inspections.reuseBasis: W3C Document Licence. Reference-only; specification text is not copied into artifacts.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That a set of provenance descriptions can be named and treated as an entity in its own right, so that the provenance of provenance can be expressed and a reader can ask who asserted a given account.
inspections.boundary: A model for expressing provenance, not a guarantee of it. Naming a bundle does not make its contents accurate, and the specification does not establish that any recorded graph is complete.
inspections.relationshipToEarlier: Same Recommendation inspected in Tranche 13 for compiler provenance and citation lineage, read here at the bundle definition.
